summary: Thread metadata follows causal edits and fences the complete effective snapshot; require current readers and storage version 23.

replay.detail: Existing immutable metadata claims retain their bodies and predecessor links. The reader selects causal successors before canonical concurrent ties and versions the effective creation, title, lifecycle and frontier, including repaired-source exclusion. No stored history or pairing record is rewritten.

schema.detail: Published main storage version 20 advances to 23 using the existing normal open path; private version-21/22 reader pilots also upgrade through it. The floor adds no table migration or claim field. Earlier serving binaries refuse the upgraded store. The message envelope marker remains thread_reader_version 2.

rules.detail: Typed metadata CAS checks the opaque complete snapshot and appends all effective causal frontier parents atomically. Existing authority and idempotency-recovery checks remain. Reader readiness 3 is required for typed writes; versions 1 and 2 cannot activate them.

compatibility.detail: Upgrade every current client and serving member together. Lifecycle action receipts expose immutable metadata_claim_id, with no metadata_revision alias; subsequent CAS fences use the observed ThreadSummary.revision. Stored claim readers and existing pairing admission/migration policy remain, without converting ambiguous historical grants into authority.

downtime.detail: Restart each serving daemon into the current reader release before activating typed writes. Opening the store completes the existing upgrade and stamps version 23; retain the matching pre-upgrade backup for recovery.

manual.detail: Before writes, directly verify the current build and reader-readiness v3 on every serving/configured member. Historical startup advertisements alone are insufficient deployment evidence. Keep fresh old readers out of the serving fleet: the same-store version floor does not fence a fresh network member.

recovery.detail: Roll forward with a current binary. Do not lower user_version or run an older binary against upgraded state. Any rollback must use a consistent pre-upgrade backup with its matching binary and existing runtime/authority recovery requirements; preserve the upgraded history and pairing evidence.
